meta.title: Tech hiring isn't shrinking. It's moving.
meta.summary: Demand has shifted toward AI, data, cloud and systems roles and away from entry-level and generic software roles. By location it is moving toward the US South and Northeast, India's captive engineering centers, the Gulf and nearshore hubs. This page summarizes figures from public sources as of the date above.

locations.name: United States
locations.headline: Recovering from a low base
locations.evidence: Active IT postings reached 625,633 in September 2026, the highest in over three years and up 22.4% year over year. Software postings still sit about 25% below February 2020.

locations.name: India: GCCs
locations.headline: Record hiring at multinationals' captive centers
locations.evidence: Projected 2026 hiring is 510,452, 3.4 times the 2021 level. 64% of new roles require AI, data science or automation skills, while overall white-collar hiring fell 9% year over year in June.

locations.name: India: IT services
locations.headline: Recovering after a weak FY26
locations.evidence: The top five firms added 13,918 people in Q2 FY27 (July to September 2026) and 24,398 in the first half, against 2,689 a year earlier. Wipro shed 6,716.

locations.name: United Kingdom
locations.headline: Software postings up year over year
locations.evidence: The US and UK are the only two large markets where software vacancies are still climbing, per an Indeed-based analysis from May 2026.

locations.name: Germany
locations.headline: About half the pre-pandemic level
locations.evidence: Software postings are down 4 to 6% year over year, and the Indeed index sits near 50 against a February 2020 baseline of 100.

locations.name: France
locations.headline: Slipping year over year
locations.evidence: Software postings are down 4 to 6% over the past 12 months.

locations.name: Canada
locations.headline: Flat, with a surplus of software developers
locations.evidence: Software postings are flat year over year. All tech postings were 19% below early 2020 as of August 2025, a milder fall than in the US, UK or France. Job Bank rates the Toronto outlook for developers as very limited.

locations.name: Australia
locations.headline: Above its 2020 baseline
locations.evidence: Australia is the notable exception among tracked countries: software postings stayed above their February 2020 level.

locations.name: Gulf: UAE and Saudi Arabia
locations.headline: Fastest-growing new hub for AI and data
locations.evidence: UAE hiring grew 39% and Saudi Arabia 26% in 2025. Data scientist hiring rose 43% and AI engineer hiring 31% from 2024 to 2025. Saudi online hiring slipped 1% year over year in August 2026.

locations.name: Southeast Asia
locations.headline: Offshore and engineering hub growth
locations.evidence: Recruiters describe Vietnam as the software-engineering center and the Philippines moving into cybersecurity and fintech. Philippine offshoring is forecast to reach $61 billion by 2030 and add nearly 1 million jobs.

locations.name: Latin America
locations.headline: Nearshore hiring for US companies
locations.evidence: Mexico, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina are the main nearshore markets, with senior developers costing 30 to 50% less than US peers. Colombia overtook Argentina as the top hiring destination.

roles.name: AI/ML engineers and AI-skilled roles
roles.headline: Fastest-growing family
roles.evidence: US AI/ML job titles nearly tripled since May 2024 (13,636 active postings). India GCC AI, data and analytics hiring grew 38%. UAE AI engineer hiring grew 31%.
roles.where: US (TX, CA, NY, Seattle), Bengaluru and Hyderabad, UAE

roles.name: Data scientists, analysts and engineers
roles.headline: Growing, with real shortages
roles.evidence: Data analysts rank fourth by US posting volume. Gulf data scientist hiring rose 43%. A report cites a 43% supply gap for AI and data analytics talent in India.

roles.name: Cloud, DevOps, platform and systems
roles.headline: Steady to rising
roles.evidence: Systems engineers rank second and DevOps engineers fifth by US posting volume. A report cites a 38% supply gap in platform engineering in India.

roles.name: Cybersecurity
roles.headline: Record openings, fewer generic postings
roles.evidence: CyberSeek counts 514,359 US openings in the 12 months to March 2026, up 12%. CyberSN counts postings down 26.4% in January to September 2026, while AI security engineer demand rose 268.3%.

roles.name: General software engineers
roles.headline: Recovering, still below peak
roles.evidence: Still the most-posted US tech role, with 47,598 new openings in September, but about 25% below the February 2020 level. Up in the UK, down in Germany and France.

roles.name: Tech support
roles.headline: Steady, high volume
roles.evidence: Third by US posting volume in September 2026.

roles.name: Entry-level and junior roles
roles.headline: Weakest segment almost everywhere
roles.evidence: US senior postings are up 13.5% since January 2025 while entry-level postings are down 6.3%. India GCC hiring of 0 to 3 year professionals is the exception, up 18%.

entryLevel.note: No official ranking exists. This order combines one US postings study with survey and platform data; ranks three to five are a judgment call.

items.evidence: Highest entry and junior share of postings, 21.8%, in 20,867 US tech postings from March to May 2026.
Most volume (6,681 postings in that dataset) and a 14.3% entry share, but a shrinking slice of new-grad hiring: 6.2% of hires in 2022, 5.4% in 2026.
Described as the one IT role that routinely hires people with no experience. Tech-support postings were reported up 16.1% from January to April 2026.
High demand, but postings labeled entry level often ask for 3+ years of experience.

Fastest growing from a small base. AI engineer tops LinkedIn's fast-growing entry-level list, and 49% of surveyed hiring managers named AI security and risk analyst the most in-demand entry-level AI role.

entryLevel.lateral: Platform engineer, SRE, backend engineer and ML engineer are more often lateral moves than first jobs.
entryLevel.context: Only 12.5% of software and ICT postings are entry level, against 38.3% across all occupations.

caveats: Postings are not hires. CompTIA's research lead warns that postings do not always lead to hiring.
Sources conflict. Early-2026 layoff counts range from about 45,000 to 78,557 because trackers and time windows differ.
There is no like-for-like India index. The Indeed Hiring Lab trackers used here do not include India, so India figures come from foundit, company filings and recruiter surveys.
Confidence labels: High is a primary source, Medium is a published tracker or press report, Low is a recruiter or staffing vendor with a commercial interest.
